subject: Request: throughput & latency exception for IonWave pilot — temporary velocity allowance
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@ionwave.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@ionwave.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot go-live — request for temporary throughput & latency allowance

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. IonWave is targeting a limited pilot of our clinical triage assistant starting next Monday (9/20). We expect an initial ramp that will spike well above our baseline quota for a short window as clinicians run batch assessments over seeded patient cohorts.

Quick ask: can Redwood grant a temporary throughput buffer and a tighter latency guardrail for the pilot window (9/20–9/23)? The pilot is latency-sensitive for clinical workflows — target P95 <= 300ms — and we’d like a temporary pool of tokens or a short-lived exception to the normal fairness throttling so the pilot doesn’t get rate-limited during live sessions.

Attached is a short traffic forecast and a one-page pilot plan. If this needs procurement/contract language we can loop Samir. We’re flexible on billing for burst usage but would like a clear SLA and a defined rollback/failover policy.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, IonWave Therapeutics
Attachment: IonWave_Pilot_Traffic_Forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@ionwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot go-live — request for temporary throughput & latency allowance

Hi Elena — appreciate the heads up and the forecast.

High level: we can support a transient increase in throughput and a tightened latency objective for a short pilot, but we need to lock a few operational controls first so we don’t impact multi-tenant fairness or violate uptime SLOs for other customers.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Marcus to validate capacity for your forecasted peak and propose a priority token pool vs. short-term quota uplift.
- Monica to confirm billing and procurement path (amendment vs. pilot addendum).
- We’ll draft a 3–4 day SLA addendum with explicit thresholds, breach remedies (credits), and automatic rollback triggers.

Can you confirm: expected requests/sec at peak, median seq length, and whether you will use streaming responses? Also confirm the exact pilot window you want Redwood to treat as elevated (your note mentions 9/20–9/23).

I’ll pull legal into the draft only after Marcus and Monica sign off on the operational approach.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@ionwave.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot go-live — request for temporary throughput & latency allowance

Elena / team — reviewing the forecast now. A few technical notes from infra:

- Priority token pool is our preferred approach for short windows (keeps fairness intact). We can create a time-bound token pool of N tokens attached to your account for 72 hours.
- To meet a P95 <= 300ms at peak we need: peak TPS, average prompt length (tokens), and whether you’ll use streaming. Long generation + streaming increases I/O and latencies.
- If you’re running many concurrent sessions with long context, we recommend a light quantization model variant for this pilot to reduce inference time. We can pin to a compatible quantized build for the window.

Estimate (ballpark) based on the spreadsheet: for a 15k req/day concentrated into 72 hours, we’d provision an extra 2–4 GPU-hours per day and a token pool of ~120M tokens. I’ll attach a short capacity estimate.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_estimate_marcus_v1.pdf (est.)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@ionwave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@ionwave.com>, procurement@ionwave.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot go-live — request for temporary throughput & latency allowance

Thanks Marcus — that estimate aligns with our internal numbers. A couple clarifications from procurement:

- We want explicit breach remedies if latency > 500ms P95 during the pilot: propose 20% service credit on pilot fees for any day that misses the target.
- We need a one-paragraph amendment to the MSA that notes the temporary exception window and rollback triggers (e.g., sustained cluster contention > 60% for 30m).
- DocuSign is preferable for the amendment. I can share the procurement contact (Samir copied).

Samir, are there any internal PO constraints or timing issues we should flag?

— Elena
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@ionwave.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@ionwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot go-live — request for temporary throughput & latency allowance

Samir / Elena — attaching a short proposed amendment and the operational playbook for the elevated window. Key points in the draft:

- Window: 2026-09-20T00:00:00 - 2026-09-23T23:59:59 (PST)
- Elevated token pool: 120,000,000 tokens allocated to IonWave for the window (time-bound, non-rollover)
- Latency objective: P95 <= 300ms; breach threshold for credits: P95 > 500ms for a sustained 1-hour period triggers a 20% credit for that calendar day
- Rollback: automatic reversion to standard fair-share throttling if cluster contention > 60% sustained for 30 minutes, or a manual rollback request from IonWave ops
- Billing: usage billed to the normal rate; credits applied to pilot invoices for qualifying breaches

Monica — can you confirm if the billing path is an amendment to the existing PO or a standalone pilot invoice? Once Monica confirms we can route to Legal and DocuSign.

Best,
— Hannah
Attachment: Proposed_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx (draft amendment)
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@ionwave.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@ionwave.com>
Cc: procurement@ionwave.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot go-live — request for temporary throughput & latency allowance

Hannah — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear draft. Procurement is good with the amendment language as long as we get a DocuSign link today and a final invoice showing pilot fees + potential credit calculation.

We’ll sign the amendment and issue an expedited PO. Start date of 9/20 works for us. Please include a short runbook for rollback and an on-call contact during the pilot window.

Samir Patel
Sr. Manager, Procurement, IonWave Therapeutics
procurement@ionwave.com
Attachment: (none)
